note: Human-reviewed DUPLICATE THESIS RECORDS — one physical submission that Estudo Geral deposited twice, so the corpus counts a thesis that does not exist. Each entry names the record the build DROPS (`duplicate_handle`), the record that STAYS (`kept_handle`), and the front-matter fields the verdict rests on (`identical_fields`), which analysis/duplicate_theses.py re-proves equal on EVERY build — if the two records stop matching in those fields, the reviewed verdict is no longer the one a human reached and the build stops. The key is a THESIS HANDLE and the claim is only "this record is not a distinct thesis": an entry never says whose thesis anything is and must never grow a person field, which is the same line data/person_aliases.json, data/person_full_names.json and data/multi_thesis_authors.json draw — option C, the thesis-name -> person lookup, is rejected (docs/thesis-attribution.md). Nothing here DETECTS anything. The rule version of this file ("byte-identical abstracts are the same thesis") was weighed and rejected: the duplicate below was measured as the only (author, date) pair spanning more than one handle across all 2690 harvested theses, so a detector would solve a problem measured as not existing, and its false positives would silently delete real theses — in this corpus similarity is not identity. The .md file and its manifest entry are NOT deleted: analysis/build_thesis_facts.py's reconcile() still runs over the full harvested corpus and the exclusion applies immediately after it, so the exclusion can never be mistaken for a harvest gap, and reverting it is deleting one entry here and rebuilding. Consequence worth knowing when auditing: `ls estudo_geral/*.md | wc -l` is now legitimately one higher than `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM theses`; the build report's `duplicate_theses.excluded_handles` is the breadcrumb. See analysis/duplicate_theses.py and docs/design/uc-phd-duplicate-thesis-exclusion.md.

entries.evidence: One doctoral thesis deposited as two Estudo Geral records. Both OAI records read directly on 2026-10-19 (https://estudogeral.uc.pt/oai/request, verb=GetRecord, metadataPrefix=oai_dc, identifier=oai:estudogeral.uc.pt:10316/90536 and .../10316/90537): both are `info:eu-repo/semantics/doctoralThesis`, both dc:creator "Moio, Isabel Sofia Fernandes", both dc:date 2018-01-09, and both carry the SAME THREE dc:description values byte for byte — the degree note ("Tese de Doutoramento em Ciências da Educação, especialidade em Educação de Adultos...", sha1 a8d10e26406e4f63), the 4712-char Portuguese abstract (sha1 c16a2ee353484e19) and the 4437-char English abstract (sha1 008a69c144ba576b). The record that settles it: 10316/90536's OAI record carries TWO dc:title values, the second of which is "Reconhecimento de Competências no Ensino Superior: uma realidade reconhecida ou a reconhecer?" — 10316/90537's title exactly. The two records are the same thesis under two handles, and 90536's harvested `title` field (literally "Isabel Sofia Fernandes Moio", the author's own name) is this repo's extractor taking the first of those two dc:title values. 90537 is the record with the catalogue identifier (dc:identifier 101568410) alongside its handle; 90536 has only its handle. Both records list the identical four oai_sets (com_10316_266, com_10316_15517, col_10316_200, col_10316_15519), i.e. the duplicate is not a cross-listing artefact of the harvest's set expansion. Scope checked, not assumed: a corpus-wide scan for any (author, date) pair spanning more than one handle across all 2690 harvested theses found this pair and no other (Debugger, Kanban card 3fe5bf3b-9510-8137-b4cc-f53bbbbe4ec4, comment of 2026-10-19 07:41; re-confirmed against the committed seed on 2026-10-19). The fields that DIFFER are all name/keyword FORM, not content, and are consistent with one deposit catalogued twice: the same two supervisors in fuller legal form on 90536 ("Alcoforado, Joaquim Luís Medeiros" / "Vieira, Cristina Maria Coimbra") vs short form on 90537, and the same five keyword concepts as bilingual-combined strings on 90536 vs ten separate PT/EN strings on 90537.
entries.note: 10316/90537 is the record that stays: it carries the real title, the same content, and the catalogue identifier. The malformed title on 90536 is moot once the record is dropped — fixing the extractor's two-dc:title handling is deliberately out of scope for the card that added this file (PO scope, docs/design/uc-phd-duplicate-thesis-exclusion.md §4), and would only ever have produced a second record with the right title rather than removing the duplicate.
